title: Habakkuk Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Habakkuk chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Habakkuk Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Habakkuk Chapter 2.

questions.question: What does Habakkuk say he will do upon his watch?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk states in Habakkuk 2:1, 'I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower...'

questions.question: Who answered Habakkuk when he was watching?
questions.explanation: In Habakkuk 2:2, it is the LORD who answered Habakkuk, saying, 'Write the vision...'

questions.question: What is the purpose of writing the vision according to Habakkuk?
options: To make it plain upon tables
questions.correctAnswer: To make it plain upon tables
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:2 states that the vision should be written plainly so that 'he may run that readeth it.'

questions.question: According to Habakkuk, what should one do if the vision tarries?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:3 encourages waiting for the vision, stating, 'though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come...'

questions.question: True or False: The just shall live by their faith according to Habakkuk.
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:4 states, 'the just shall live by his faith.' This confirms the statement is true.

questions.question: What does Habakkuk say about the proud man in verse 5?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:5 describes a man who transgresses by wine as a proud man.

questions.question: True or False: The proud man does not keep at home according to Habakkuk.
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:5 states that the proud man 'neither keepeth at home,' making the statement true.

questions.question: What will happen to those who take up a parable against the proud man?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:7 indicates that those who take up a parable against the proud man shall rise up suddenly.

questions.question: True or False: The proud man increases that which is his according to Habakkuk.
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:6 warns against him that increaseth that which is not his, so the statement is false.

questions.question: In Habakkuk 2, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk begins the chapter by stating, 'I will stand upon my watch' in Habakkuk 2:1.

questions.question: What does Habakkuk say will cover the earth?
options: The knowledge of the glory of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The knowledge of the glory of the LORD
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:14 states, 'For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD...'

medium.title: Habakkuk Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Habakkuk Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Habakkuk 2:8, what will happen to those who spoil many nations?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:8 states that because of the violence inflicted on others, the remnant of the people will spoil those who have spoiled them.

questions.question: What is warned against in Habakkuk 2:9 regarding covetousness?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:9 warns that coveting an evil covetousness leads to shame and is destructive to one's house and soul.

questions.question: True or False: Habakkuk 2:12 states that building a town with blood is acceptable if it leads to prosperity.
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:12 declares woe to those who build a town with blood, indicating that such actions are wrong and unacceptable.

questions.question: What does Habakkuk 2:10 suggest about the consequences of cutting off many people?
questions.explanation: According to Habakkuk 2:10, consulting shame by harming others results in sinning against one's own soul, thus bringing shame.

questions.question: What does Habakkuk 2:13 reveal about laboring for vanity?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:13 indicates that laboring in vain is ultimately unprofitable, as it does not yield any true benefit.

questions.question: True or False: Habakkuk 2:14 proclaims that the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord.
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:14 indeed states that the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord, affirming God's ultimate plan.

questions.question: What does Habakkuk 2:11 imply about the consequences of wrongdoing?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:11 implies that even inanimate objects like stones and beams will cry out against wrongdoing, indicating accountability.

questions.question: How does Habakkuk 2:12 connect the act of building with blood to God's judgment?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:12 warns that building a city through iniquity is subject to God's judgment, indicating that it will lead to destruction.

questions.question: In what way does Habakkuk 2:15 caution against leading others to drunkenness?
options: It is a sign of friendship
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:15 warns that giving drink to a neighbor in order to exploit them leads to shame for the giver.

questions.question: True or False: Habakkuk 2:19 states that graven images can provide guidance to those who trust in them.
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:19 indicates that graven images are worthless and cannot provide guidance, emphasizing their emptiness.

questions.question: What does Habakkuk 2:16 say about the shame that will come upon the proud?
options: They will be filled with shame
questions.correctAnswer: They will be filled with shame
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:16 states that the proud will be filled with shame, reversing their glory and leading to their downfall.

questions.question: What does Habakkuk 2:3 encourage believers to do while waiting for God's vision?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:3 encourages believers to wait for the appointed time of God's vision, assuring them that it will surely come.

hard.title: Habakkuk Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Habakkuk Chapter 2.

questions.question: What did the LORD instruct Habakkuk to do with the vision?
questions.explanation: The LORD told Habakkuk to 'Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables' (Habakkuk 2:2).

questions.question: According to Habakkuk 2:4, how shall the just live?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'but the just shall live by his faith' (Habakkuk 2:4).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a consequence of pride in Habakkuk 2:5?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that the proud man 'cannot be satisfied' (Habakkuk 2:5).

questions.question: What will happen to those who spoil nations according to Habakkuk 2:8?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee' (Habakkuk 2:8).

questions.question: True or False: The earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD as per Habakkuk 2:14.
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:14 states, 'For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD.'

questions.question: What does Habakkuk 2:19 warn against regarding idols?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; ... it shall teach!' (Habakkuk 2:19).

questions.question: What literary device is used in Habakkuk 2:15-16 regarding drinking?
questions.explanation: The structure of the 'Woe' statements creates a chiasm, emphasizing the consequences of drunkenness (Habakkuk 2:15-16).

questions.question: True or False: The stone and the timber will cry out against those who commit iniquity according to Habakkuk 2:11.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For the stone shall cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the timber shall answer it' (Habakkuk 2:11).

questions.question: Which other scripture echoes the theme of living by faith found in Habakkuk 2:4?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:17 states, 'The just shall live by faith,' echoing Habakkuk 2:4.

questions.question: What will cover the proud according to Habakkuk 2:17?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'For the violence of Lebanon shall cover thee' (Habakkuk 2:17).

questions.question: What does the term 'dumb idols' in Habakkuk 2:18 imply about their nature?
questions.explanation: 'Dumb idols' signifies they cannot speak or have life, as stated in Habakkuk 2:18.

questions.question: Which concept from Habakkuk 2:20 emphasizes the sovereignty of God?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:20 highlights the LORD being in His holy temple, emphasizing His sovereignty and presence.

questions.question: Which biblical theme is reflected in Habakkuk 2:13 about human efforts?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'the people shall labour in the very fire, and the people shall weary themselves for very vanity' (Habakkuk 2:13).

theological.title: Habakkuk Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Habakkuk Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Habakkuk 2:4 teach about the relationship between faith and righteousness?
options: The just shall live by faith
The just shall perish by pride
The just shall be judged by actions
The just shall live by law
questions.correctAnswer: The just shall live by faith
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:4 states, 'but the just shall live by his faith,' emphasizing that righteousness is attained through faith rather than through works or pride.

questions.question: In Habakkuk 2:5, how is the proud man characterized?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:5 describes the proud man as one who 'gathereth unto him all nations,' indicating his insatiable desire and ambition.

questions.question: What does the vision in Habakkuk 2:3 signify about God's timing?
options: God's timing is perfect and appointed
questions.correctAnswer: God's timing is perfect and appointed
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:3 says, 'For the vision is yet for an appointed time,' indicating that God's plans and revelations have a divine timetable.

questions.question: According to Habakkuk 2:6, what will happen to those who increase what is not theirs?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:6 mentions that those who increase what is not theirs will face a taunting proverb, illustrating the consequences of their actions.

questions.question: What is the main consequence outlined in Habakkuk 2:8 for those who spoil many nations?
options: They will be blessed with riches
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee,' indicating that those who commit violence will ultimately face the same fate.

questions.question: What does Habakkuk 2:14 reveal about the knowledge of the Lord?
options: It will be limited to Israel
It will only be known by the wise
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:14 states, 'For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD,' signifying a future where God's presence and knowledge are pervasive.

questions.question: In Habakkuk 2:12, what is said about building a town with blood?
questions.explanation: The verse declares, 'Woe to him that buildeth a town with blood,' indicating that such actions are wicked and contrary to God's will.

questions.question: How does Habakkuk 2:19 criticize idolatry?
options: It is a source of power
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:19 states, 'Behold, it is laid over with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in the midst of it,' criticizing the futility of trusting in idols.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can be derived from combining Habakkuk 2:3 and 2:14?
options: God's glory will not be revealed
Faith in God's promises leads to knowledge of His glory
Human efforts can achieve God's purposes
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in God's promises leads to knowledge of His glory
questions.explanation: The combined teaching emphasizes that while God's vision may tarry, it ultimately leads to the revelation of His glory throughout the earth.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated in Habakkuk 2:20?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:20 states, 'But the LORD is in his holy temple,' indicating God's holiness and the reverence due to Him by all creation.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'the cup of the LORD's right hand' in Habakkuk 2:16?
questions.explanation: The phrase points to God's divine judgment against the proud and wicked, as indicated by the context of the verse.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Habakkuk 2:10 and 2:12 convey about sin and its consequences?
options: Sin brings shame and violence upon a community
questions.correctAnswer: Sin brings shame and violence upon a community
questions.explanation: These verses illustrate that sin, particularly against others, invites judgment and destruction upon the ungodly.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not address injustice. What does Habakkuk 2:8 actually teach?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:8 teaches that those who have spoiled many nations will themselves be spoiled, indicating God's justice in addressing wrongdoing.

questions.question: How does Habakkuk 2:7 speak to the inevitability of divine retribution?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:7 indicates that retribution will arise suddenly against the proud, emphasizing the certainty and swiftness of divine justice.

questions.question: What does Habakkuk 2:11 imply about the inanimate creation's testimony against sin?
options: It is indifferent to human actions
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 2:11 states that 'the stone shall cry out of the wall,' suggesting that creation itself testifies against those who commit injustice.
